Class DatabaseRepository

java.lang.Object
org.mavendb.loader.DatabaseRepository
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
class DatabaseRepository extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Repository for database operations with support for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, DuckDB, MongoDB and OpenSearch. Handles all persistent storage operations for Maven records and documents.

Connections are reused across batches: SQL writers borrow an idle connection (or open a new one) and return it after commit, so at most one connection exists per concurrent writer. MongoDB uses one shared, thread-safe MongoClient; OpenSearch one shared OpenSearchClient.

    • storeCopyData

      protected void storeCopyData(byte[] copyData, int size, long counter)
      Store a batch of rows in COPY text format with the database's bulk load statement: COPY ... FROM STDIN for PostgreSQL, LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE for MySQL and MariaDB.

      The server parses and inserts the rows as one stream: no per-row Bind/Execute round trip (PostgreSQL), no multi-row INSERT text to build in the driver and parse on the server (MySQL).

      Parameters:
      copyData - Rows in COPY text format, see toCopyData(List, DatabaseType)
      size - Number of rows in copyData, for checking and logging
      counter - Record counter for logging
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the batch could not be written; the transaction is rolled back

    • storeDuckDB

      protected void storeDuckDB(List<DatabaseRepository.SqlRow> rows, long counter)
      Store a DuckDB batch with the Appender: the rows go straight into DuckDB's column vectors, with no SQL to build or parse.

      Each writer has its own connection and appender; DuckDB appends from several connections concurrently.

      Parameters:
      rows - Prepared rows to persist, see toSQLRow(Document)
      counter - Record counter for logging
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the batch could not be written; the transaction is rolled back

    • loadDataLocal

      private long loadDataLocal(Connection conn, byte[] copyData) throws SQLException
      Run LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE with the rows streamed from memory.

      With LOCAL, MySQL and MariaDB turn data errors (truncation, bad values, duplicate keys) into warnings and carry on, so any warning fails the batch instead of silently storing altered rows.

      Returns:
      Number of rows loaded
      Throws:
      SQLException

    • toCopyData

      protected static byte[] toCopyData(List<DatabaseRepository.SqlRow> rows, DatabaseType dbType)
      Encode prepared rows in COPY text format (tab separated, \N for null), UTF-8.

      PostgreSQL COPY and MySQL/MariaDB LOAD DATA read the same format and escapes; only booleans differ: t/f for PostgreSQL, 1/0 for the MySQL/MariaDB BOOLEAN (TINYINT) columns.

      Thread safe: called on the conversion threads, so the writer only streams bytes.

      Parameters:
      rows - Rows prepared by toSQLRow(Document)
      dbType - DatabaseType.PSQL, DatabaseType.MYSQL or DatabaseType.MARIADB
      Returns:
      COPY data for storeCopyData(byte[], int, long)

    • createIndexOpenSearch

      protected void createIndexOpenSearch(String indexId) throws IOException
      Drop and create the OpenSearch index from db/opensearch/create.json, ready for the bulk load.

      The definition is tuned for loading, finishOpenSearch(String) restores the search settings:

      • 8 primary shards: indexing runs in parallel on a multi-core node; no replicas on a single node
      • refresh_interval: -1: no new searchable segments while loading
      • translog.durability: async: no fsync per bulk request; a crash during the load means a rerun
      • best_compression: smaller index for the export; the large OSGi headers compress well
      • Explicit mappings: identifiers are keyword (exact match, aggregations), names, descriptions and OSGi headers are text (full text search), timestamps are dates. Other strings are keyword, not the default text plus keyword pair, which would index each value twice
      Parameters:
      indexId - Maven index id, like central
      Throws:
      IOException
